title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + a deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.018796992481203034; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked for 6 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not recorded in per‑task artifacts and thus could not be evaluated. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed absolute improvement is small and did not meet the preregistered α=0.05 decision rule. We provide preregistered design details, deterministic validator semantics, complete numeric outcomes, representative artifact‑grounded repair examples (e.g., task-000008), contamination findings (no exact public duplicates flagged), and an evidence‑grounded discussion of limitations and implications.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→CLI translation, zero‑touch configuration synthesis, and automated maintenance workflows [1]. Stochastic generation can produce syntactic or semantic violations—missing commands, unsafe operation orderings, or constraint breaches—that create operational risk when applied to device CLIs. To reduce that risk, pipelines that interpose deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish‑style analysis) and bounded repair loops (generate–verify–repair, GVR) have been proposed as a way to provide deterministic acceptance criteria for candidate outputs [2,3,4].

This study addresses the preregistered question (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1): Does a GVR pipeline that uses a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), a deterministic Batfish‑style validator, and at most one automated LLM repair call reduce deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures relative to the same initial candidate without repair? The design isolates the effect of the allowed validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), consistent with the registered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline.
sections.related_work:
Prior work documents early LLM uses for NetOps, intent→CLI translation benchmarks and the need for verification/grounding when moving toward automation [1,2]. Generate–verify–repair ideas have been explored in code and regulated domains as a mechanism to obtain deterministic validation via external oracles and bounded repair loops [3]. Batfish and header‑space analyzers provide deterministic reachability and sequencing checks suitable as oracles in LLM‑augmented NetOps prototypes; their primitives and historical use motivate the validator selection in our study [4]. Analyses of what LLMs need to synthesize correct router configurations highlight sequencing and vendor‑syntax difficulties and thus support verifier augmentation [5].

Our contribution is an artifact‑archived, preregistered paired test that (a) follows shared_initial_candidate semantics per the preregistration, (b) archives raw model traces and deterministic validator traces for auditability, and (c) reports exact paired contingency counts and both exact and bootstrap inferential summaries according to the registered analysis plan.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study preregistration is identified as cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under these semantics the same single sampled initial model candidate is used to compute both the baseline outcome (single‑shot candidate → validator pass/fail) and the guarded outcome (same candidate → validator; if it fails, at most one automated LLM repair is permitted; final validator pass/fail recorded). This paired design isolates the effect of the permitted validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial candidate.

Task bank and sampling: The preregistered task bank deterministically produced 300 intent→CLI pairs: 150 Cisco‑like and 150 Juniper‑like items, combining public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator (generator id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Per‑task manifests, generation seeds, and the inclusion/exclusion logic are archived. Inclusion/exclusion, retry, and missingness rules followed the preregistration; deterministic exclusion rules removed 34 both‑arm provider/model failures, yielding 266 complete pairs for the primary analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model, orchestration, and sampling: The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Archived model configuration includes max_output_tokens = 1024, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = openai_responses, and temperature = null (unset). The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Provider call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 306 with 34 failed calls. Stage accounting recorded shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6.

Deterministic validator: The binary oracle used is deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each candidate it executes CLI syntactic parsing/normalization, checks the preregistered required_sequence against parsed commands, enforces allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields constraints, and evaluates reachability/ordering on the synthetic topology model. Episode artifacts archive validation_before and validation_after traces that include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation codes, and normalized_configuration (see execution/scoring/*.json for per‑episode traces). The validator’s binary pass/fail is the primary endpoint.

Repair loop and mechanics: Per the preregistration the initial sampled candidate is shared across both arms (shared_initial_candidate). If the deterministic validator fails that candidate, the guarded arm may invoke at most one automated LLM repair call. The repair prompt exposes the validator failure codes and task constraints and requests a corrected configuration; repair prompts and provider traces are archived when invoked. The single‑repair bound was chosen to model a constrained automated correction stage before escalation.

Analysis plan: Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two‑sided on paired binary outcomes at α=0.05. Interval estimation: paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) for the paired difference as preregistered. Rationale: exact McNemar is the preregistered hypothesis test; because McNemar p‑values are discrete and depend only on discordant counts, we preregistered a paired bootstrap CI to separately quantify the magnitude and sampling uncertainty of the paired difference. Secondary estimands (preregistered) included median_repair_iterations_per_task and median end‑to‑end latency (latency could not be evaluated because it was not recorded per episode). Missingness handling: complete_pair_primary rule excluded 34 both‑arm provider/model failures from the primary test; sensitivity analyses treat these conservatively as failures.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: Planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 532; failed episodes = 68. Complete paired units analysed = 266; both_missing_pairs = 34 excluded per preregistration (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider/model call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 272. Repair stage calls recorded = 6.

Primary outcomes (complete_pairs = 266): baseline successes = 260; guarded final successes = 265. Paired contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 260 (both pass), n10 = 5 (guarded pass only), n01 = 0 (baseline pass only), n00 = 1 (both fail). Observed proportions: baseline = 260/266 = 0.9774436090; guarded = 265/266 = 0.9962406015. Paired difference = 0.018796992481203034. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered α=0.05 decision rule → not significant). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records bootstrap parameters). The discrete‑discordant nature of McNemar explains why the bootstrap CI may exclude zero while the exact McNemar p‑value does not reject at α=0.05.

Repair behavior and representative artifacts: Repairs were invoked for 6 tasks (repair stage_count = 6); median repair iterations per task = 0. Representative example: task-000008 shared initial candidate (execution/responses/task-000008-shared-initial.txt, sha256 = 89306095ceeedc3df7d752beb035f342edf9e82b7252e45356919e29958245e7) contained an incomplete final line "interface uplink2\n" and failed validator checks. The guarded final (execution/responses/task-000008-guarded.txt, sha256 = d52b7616f93a608409c7ce4eeb21958b8ceeb502faaf302d9b36468d8a627944) contained the repaired full sequence; validator traces (execution/scoring/task-000008-*.json) show the concrete violation codes that triggered repair and the normalized_configuration accepted after repair. All episode validator traces are archived.

Contamination and sensitivity: analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty—no exact public‑duplicate tasks were flagged and none were excluded for contamination in the primary analysis. Sensitivity treating the 34 excluded both‑arm episodes as failures (conservative N=300) yields baseline = 260/300 = 0.866667 and guarded = 265/300 = 0.883333 while yielding the same discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) and exact McNemar p = 0.0625; the primary inferential outcome is robust to the preregistered conservative missingness treatment.

Supplementary artifacts: analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv are archived with SHA‑256 values included in the execution manifest; deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms internal accounting and stage/provider call summaries used above.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute increase in validator pass‑rate (~1.88 percentage points). Under the preregistered exact‑McNemar decision rule the improvement did not reach α=0.05 (p=0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI that excludes zero highlights effect‑size uncertainty and finite‑sample behavior; because McNemar uses only discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0), its p‑value is discrete and may not reject at α=0.05 even when resampling‑based intervals suggest a positive effect. Presenting both summaries follows the preregistered analysis plan and aids readers in balancing formal hypothesis acceptance versus estimated effect magnitude.

Operational interpretation and boundary conditions: The marginal benefit of the bounded automated repair was limited by a high baseline single‑shot pass rate (≈97.7%), leaving few failures for repair to correct. Repair invocations were rare (6/300), suggesting that for this model and task corpus a single sampled candidate frequently satisfies validator rules. Thus, in high first‑pass accuracy settings the incremental operational ROI of adding a bounded automated repair stage may be small; GVR is likely to be more beneficial when first‑pass accuracy is lower, validator coverage is broader, or more repair iterations are allowed.

Threats to validity: Internal validity: the estimand explicitly measures the effect of validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial sample (shared_initial_candidate semantics). It does not evaluate independent multiple draws, constrained first‑pass prompting, or different repair budgets—those were not executed under the preregistration and are outside the estimand. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic, required‑sequence, and reachability checks; semantic violations outside its rule battery are undetected and unmeasured. External validity: tasks derive from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor clusters; generalization to other vendors, larger production topologies, or differing difficulty distributions is not established. Conclusion validity: few discordant pairs (n10=5, n01=0) and the loss of 34 provider‑failure pairs reduced power and precision relative to the planned N=300.

Design lessons and recommendations grounded in artifacts: (1) Record per‑episode latency (absent in this run) to evaluate preregistered operational bounds: the preregistered H2 median latency ≤ 60 s could not be assessed because per‑task timing was not archived. (2) When baseline pass rates are high, design confirmatory studies that target lower‑baseline corpora or allow larger N to increase discordant counts and power. (3) Expand validator rule coverage and publish validator rule catalogs so that construct validity and possible verifier false negatives are auditable. (4) Compare shared_initial_candidate semantics with alternative estimands (independent multiple draws or constrained prompting) in separate preregistered arms to quantify multiple design choices rather than conflating them.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered paired experiment evaluated a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Across 266 analysed pairs the guarded pipeline improved validator pass rate by 0.018796992481203034 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625); a paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not archived and could not be assessed. All execution and analysis artifacts, including raw responses, validator traces, provider call accounting, and reconciliation manifests, are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the preregistration to support reanalysis and follow‑on studies.

Preregistration: cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Execution and analysis artifacts, logs, and hash manifests cited in this manuscript are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the preregistration for audit per the track’s reproducibility requirements.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per preregistered rules, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.

Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
Latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
